title: How Good Is DFT for Solid-Liquid Interfaces? A Comparison With the Random-Phase Approximation for Water on Graphene
authors: Xavier R. Advincula, Yair Litman, Jiuyang Shi, Flaviano Della Pia, Christoph Schran, Angelos Michaelides
abstract: Simulations of water at solid interfaces routinely disagree on basic properties, from contact angle to friction, depending on the model used, whether an empirical force field or a density functional theory (DFT) exchange-correlation (XC) approximation. Yet no accurate computational reference has been available to determine which, if any, is reliable. Here we assess XC approximations spanning the rungs of Jacob's Ladder against the random-phase approximation (RPA) at the graphene-water interface. Using machine-learned potentials (MLPs) trained on both DFT and RPA data, we achieve the extensive sampling required to characterize interfacial structure, wettability, friction, and vibrational sum-frequency generation spectra. We find that XC approximations disagree substantially with RPA and with each other. To make sense of this, we introduce a transferable, multi-observable scoring framework that distills each functional's agreement with RPA into a single measure. Six functionals emerge as reliable starting points for studies of graphene-water and other dispersion-dominated interfaces, namely B3LYP-D3(0), revPBE-D3(0), revPBE-D3(BJ), B97M-rV, r$^{2}$SCAN, and revPBE0-D3(0). Notably, this ranking follows no simple rule based on functional family or rung of Jacob's Ladder. What does hold across functionals is that dynamical and spectroscopic properties tend to be harder for DFT to reproduce than structural ones, with direct consequences for functional selection. Our framework also offers a general strategy for benchmarking any atomistic model, including the new generation of foundational MLPs, against high-accuracy references at solid--liquid interfaces. Beyond simulation, this work identifies which models can be trusted to connect measured contact angles, friction, and vibrational spectra to the molecular structure behind them.
summary: This work rigorously benchmarks various Density Functional Theory (DFT) approximations against the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) for simulating water at solid interfaces like graphene. By analyzing structure, friction, and vibrational spectra, the authors reveal significant discrepancies between models. They propose a scoring framework and identify a small set of reliable functionals for future simulations.
main_problem: Computational models for water at solid interfaces disagree significantly on fundamental properties like contact angle and friction, and no reliable computational reference exists to resolve this discrepancy.
main_result: The study identifies six specific DFT functionals that provide reliable starting points for modeling graphene-water interfaces, and shows that dynamical/spectroscopic properties are generally harder for DFT to reproduce than structural ones.
method: The authors compare various DFT exchange-correlation (XC) approximations against the high-accuracy Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) using Machine-Learned Potentials (MLPs) for extensive sampling.
model_or_system: The system studied is the solid-liquid interface, specifically water interacting with graphene. The comparison spans a wide range of computational models, including DFT functionals (Hybrids, Meta-GGAs) and the RPA reference.
key_observables: Interfacial structure (density profiles), wettability ($ho_2/ho_1$), friction coefficient ($\mu$), and vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG) spectra descriptors.
important_parameters: The comparison is benchmarked against the RPA reference level of theory, which is computationally expensive for large simulations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing a transferable, multi-observable scoring framework to quantify functional agreement with the high-accuracy RPA reference.
figures_summary: Figures compare density profiles, friction coefficients, and vibrational spectral descriptors, showing substantial quantitative deviations ($\pm 45\%$ to $\pm 230\%$) across different XC approximations relative to RPA.
paper_structure: The paper systematically assesses multiple observables (structure, friction, spectroscopy) by comparing various DFT approximations against RPA, culminating in the proposal of a scoring framework to rank functional reliability.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter/chemistry, the rigorous benchmarking methodology and the development of a general scoring framework for comparing complex quantum simulations against high-accuracy references are valuable for any field relying on multi-observable model validation.
